```data
orchestrator/jev_gate.py:488 The 'second identical attempt' override check compares only the path (`state.get("last_path") == target`), not the exact call signature. SPEC v3 requires: 'a different signature on the same path is still eligible' for suppression. Repro: session reads path P (call A, offset=0) twice -> second is suppressed, count=1, last_path=P (override not yet recorded since override only fires on the *next* repeat of A). Session then reads P at a different offset (call B) for the first time (kind=same_file_different_range, allowed), then repeats call B exactly. Call B's repeat has would_suppress=True and its signature is not in overrides and count(1) < max, but `last_path == target` is still true from A's suppression, so it is incorrectly classified as `suppression_override` and allowed through instead of being denied. This silently under-suppresses a genuinely-repeated read whenever any other range/pattern on the same file was suppressed previously in the session, contradicting the spec and none of the new tests exercise this path (test_override_disables_that_signature_for_the_session only repeats the same exact signature).
```

Planner note: the comment is right. Key the "never twice in a row" override state on the exact call signature (tool, path, range keys, pattern, flags), not on the path alone, so a different range on the same path stays eligible for suppression while the overridden signature is never suppressed again in the session. Extend tests/test_jev_gate.py::test_override_disables_that_signature_for_the_session with a different-range read on the same path after the override (it must be suppressed on its own second identical attempt).

result.summary: Fix keys the suppression-override state on the exact call signature (input_hash) instead of the file path, resolving the reported bug where a repeat on a different range/offset of the same path was incorrectly classified as an override. Minor note: the planner asked to extend test_override_disables_that_signature_for_the_session directly; the executor instead added a new test_different_signature_on_same_path_remains_eligible covering the same scenario, which is functionally equivalent and satisfies all listed acceptance criteria.
